newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ROCKIES LONG BALL DISPLAY CRUSHES ATHLETICS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ROCKIES LONG BALL DISPLAY CRUSHES ATHLETICS.

text.p: The big-hitting Colorado Rockies used the long ball to pound the Oakland Athletics 7-1 in an interleague contest on Saturday.
Ellis Burks hit a three-run homer, Larry Walker had a solo shot and Andres Galarraga added a two-run blast in a power display by Colorado.
Burks smashed a 406-foot shot to left in the third inning off Oakland starter Don Wengert (3-4) for his 15th homer to give Colorado a 4-0 lead.
"I was just trying to hit the ball hard," Burks explained. "He got it up and I just drove it out."

Carlos Reyes started the seventh inning for the A's and Walker greeted him with a towering 446-foot homer into the second deck in right field for his 19th homer of the year. Walker went 2-for-3 with three runs scored.

Oakland foiled Roger Bailey's shutout bid in the eighth when Jason McDonald singled and later scored on an errant throw by Galarraga. But Galarraga made up for his miscue by driving out his 18th homer for the final margin.
Bailey (7-5) pitched his major-league best and fifth complete game, allowing an unearned run and eight hits with four walks and five strikeouts.
Wengert (3-4) took the loss, giving up four runs and six hits. Reyes allowed three runs over the last three innings.
In Seattle, Russ Davis's solo homer off Antonio Osuna with one out in the ninth inning gave the Mariners a 9-8 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Davis crushed a 1-0 pitch over the left-field fence to end the contest. "It's probably one of the biggest thrills of my career," he said.
"Any time you can hit a game-winning home run in front of a lot of people and on national television it's special."

The Dodgers rallied from a 5-0 deficit to tie the game in the top of the eighth after a three-run seventh in which Mike Piazza belted a two-run homer followed by Eric Karros's second homer of the game.

Seattle, like the Dodgers, had 11 hits, but the Mariners had only one single, getting homers from Edger Martinez, Paul Sorrento and Ken Griffey's major league-leading 27th round tripper in addition to Davis's game-winning blast.
At Texas, Dean Palmer's three-run homer higlighted a five-run first inning and the Rangers held on for an 8-6 victory over the San Diego Padres.
Palmer's homer and a subsequent blast by Mike Simms in the first staked the Rangers to a 5-0 lead.

The game marked the first time in major-league history that the reigning MVPs went head-to-head in a regular-season contest. But San Diego's Ken Caminiti struck out four times and Texas' Juan Gonzalez also was 0-for-4.
Matt Whiteside (1-0) pitched 1 2/3 perfect innings in relief to earn the win. Danny Jackson (1-3) suffered the loss in his Padres' debut.
San Diego trailed 7-2 entering the top of the fifth but scored four times off starter Julio Santana, highlighted by Steve Finley's two-run double.
In Anaheim, Rich Aurilia belted his first career grand slam and Jeff Kent continued his torrid hitting with two homers and three RBI to power the San Francisco Giants to a 10-3 rout of the Angels.
Darryl Hamilton also homered for the Giants, who jumped out to 5-0 second-inning lead on Aurilia's big blast and Kent's first homer -- both off Anaheim starter Allen Watson.
Joe Roa (2-4), a 25-year-old rookie, earned his first win as a starter, giving up two runs and nine hits in 5 1/3 innings with no walks and four strikeouts.
Kent, who is 11-for-29 with six RBI in his last seven games, added a two-run blast off reliever Shigetoshi Hasegawa in the sixth, extending the Giants' lead to 10-1.
Watson (5-4) gave up seven runs on six hits in just 3-1/3 innings for the loss.
